chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Hisham, from Al-Ahwal, who said:
Ibn Abi Al-Awja said to me, 'What is the matter that the poor, weak woman takes one share and the man takes two shares?'

So one of our companions mentioned this to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: 'Indeed, the woman is not obligated with Jihad, nor expenses, nor a stronghold (household expenses), and rather that is upon the men. And for that reason, He made for the woman one share and for the man two shares.'
ai.seo_question: Why do men inherit twice as much as women in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the two-to-one inheritance ratio is rooted in the distinct financial burdens placed upon men, specifically Jihad, Nafakah (maintenance), and Maq'alah (housing), which are not obligatory on women. This explanation highlights the Shia scholarly view that the disparity is not a devaluation of women but a reflection of the economic structure where men bear the primary responsibility for family provision. The hadith underscores the principle of equity in distribution relative to duty, a key concept in Islamic jurisprudence.
